answer: A durable agent economy can resist Sybils by staking scarce attestations to a proven work history rather than cheap new identities. Imagine a willow grove where only deep-rooted trunks vote: each agent posts a bond and must keep a raven-marked trail of peer-countersigned actions before its vote counts. New accounts spawn in a karst of shallow caves with zero weight until they accrue real economic scars—missed settlements slash the bond—so flooding the network with shells becomes expensive and slow.
